Chapter 56: Enterprise Cloud Architecture Project Selection
Turning business constraints into a defensible cloud program
Why this chapter matters: Senior architects are evaluated on problem framing and trade-offs,
not service recall. The first project artifact must expose assumptions, stakeholders, risks and
measurable outcomes. Learning Objectives

Explain the architecture, responsibility boundaries and major trade-offs of business capability and stakeholder
analysis.

Design nonfunctional requirements and risk boundaries for enterprise scale, least privilege and bounded failure.

Implement workload portfolio and placement decisions through version-controlled automation and policy checks.

Troubleshoot architecture roadmap, funding and success measures using provider-native telemetry and
repeatable evidence.

Business capability and stakeholder analysis
Business capability and stakeholder analysis is a design boundary, not merely a console feature. In Enterprise
Cloud Architecture Project Selection, the team must document ownership, trust assumptions, dependency
direction, failure impact and the evidence used to prove the control. The recommended implementation uses
Business and technical discovery, ADRs and trade-off records, Application and data inventory, Threat, reliability
and financial models only where they satisfy an explicit requirement; equivalent services are not automatically
interchangeable. Nonfunctional requirements and risk boundaries

plane from workload execution and constrains blast radius.
